item: the panic wipe and the data-drive restart close the database to background jobs too (R689 follow-ups 1 and 4)
summary: BEFORE: R689 left two stops outside its order. The panic wipe asked no job to stop, so a job still writing could open a fresh connection after the erase and recreate the store file. The data-drive restart after a reconnect (execve) ran no stop-all, so a job was cut mid-unit and the next open rolled the unit back. NOW: after_shutdown.stop_jobs_and_close(timeout) runs the lifespan's two job steps (stop_all_jobs, then close_for_jobs whatever the wait found, even if it failed). The panic wipe runs it with ZERO wait, after holding collection (pause_for_exclusive_operation(timeout=0): the hold is never released, the corpus is gone), and also refuses the collector's own threads by name (oo-scheduler, oo-collect, oo-briefing-bg, oo-housekeeping-lane), then erases; the pool is disposed only AFTER the erase, because closing the last connection writes the log back (possibly hundreds of MiB) and that must not delay the destroyed key. No step joins a thread and a failing step never stops the wipe. Not refused, stated: the import queue, re-index managers, backup threads and request threads. The restart runs it with the graceful stop's 5 s deadline, disposes, then reaps and re-executes; a failed execve is now logged as an error, recorded as restart_failed, and ends in the shutdown instead of a restarting page that never ends. Release line: The emergency wipe now stops background work from writing before it erases, and restarting after the data drive comes back lets background work finish its current step first.
